title: National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates: Salary Sacrifice Explained for Australian Workers
description: Understand the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates. Salary sacrifice explained, plus how to convert hourly pay to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures u

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the base minimum set by the Fair Work Commission each year. Many employees are covered by a modern award that often pays more than that minimum. Award rates are industry or occupation-specific and can be higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, a retail award may have a higher base rate plus penalties for weekends or overtime. The on-site reference shows the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, while casual employees get 25% loading on top at $33.05 per hour. Always check your award or pay guide for your actual minimum.

faqs.q: How does casual loading and casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees get 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This loading is paid instead of leave entitlements. The on-site calculator has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate you enter. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading. For the National Minimum Wage, casual loading brings the rate to $33.05 per hour. Super is then paid on that casual rate at 12% on top.

faqs.q: What is salary sacrifice explained in simple terms?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice is an arrangement where you give up part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for a benefit like a car or extra super contributions. It reduces your taxable income but does not affect the ordinary earnings that super is calculated on. The calculator on this site does not deduct salary sacrifice because it varies by employer and benefit. For more details, see the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

bodyMarkdown:
## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates: Salary Sacrifice Explained

When you are comparing an hourly rate to an annual salary, the first step is to multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks in a year. This site assumes a standard full-time week of 38 hours unless you change it. That gives you the annual gross figure before tax, super, and any deductions.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. For a 38-hour week:
- Weekly gross: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90 (rounded from $1,004.92)
- Fortnightly gross: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80
- Annual gross: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80

If you are a casual employee, the Fair Work Ombudsman requires a 25% loading on top of the base rate. That makes the casual rate $33.05 per hour. The same multiplication gives:
- Weekly: $33.05 × 38 = $1,255.90
- Fortnightly: $2,511.80
- Annual: $65,306.80

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the floor. Many employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or job. For instance, the General Retail Industry Award 2020 has a higher base rate for a retail employee Level 1 than the National Minimum Wage. Award rates also include penalty rates for evenings, weekends, and public holidays. The on-site reference tables at [pay guides](/blog) can help you find your award, but always check the Fair Work Ombudsman website for the latest.

If you are not covered by an award, your minimum is the National Minimum Wage. Some enterprise agreements or individual contracts may pay more. The average full-time adult ordinary time earnings from the Australian Bureau of Statistics for May 2026 are $2,083.70 per week, which is well above the minimum. That figure is an average, not a median for your job.

### Casual Loading Explained

Casual loading is the 25% extra paid to casual employees instead of paid leave (annual leave, sick leave, etc.). The calculator on this site has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate you enter. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading. If you are a casual, check the box and the calculator will apply the loading automatically.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. For the National Minimum Wage:
- Annual super: $52,254.80 × 12% = $6,270.58
- But the maximum contribution base for super is $270,830 per quarter (2026–27). If your earnings exceed that, super stops on the excess. Most minimum wage workers will not reach that cap.

Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra contribution to your super fund. The calculator shows an estimate of super based on 12% of ordinary earnings, but it does not account for salary sacrifice or other arrangements.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. For a full-time minimum wage earner ($52,254.80), tax would be approximately:
- Taxable income $52,254.80
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: ($45,000 - $18,200) × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $52,254.80: ($52,254.80 - $45,000) × 30% = $2,176.44
- Total tax: $6,196.44
- Medicare (2%): $1,045.10
- Total deductions: $7,241.54
- Annual take-home: $52,254.80 - $7,241.54 = $45,013.26
- Weekly take-home: $45,013.26 ÷ 52 = $865.64

This is an estimate. It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice.

### Salary Sacrifice Explained

Salary sacrifice is an arrangement where you agree to receive less salary in exchange for a benefit, such as a car, laptop, or extra super contributions. The benefit is paid from your pre-tax salary, reducing your taxable income. However, salary sacrifice does not reduce the ordinary earnings that your super guarantee is calculated on. The Australian Taxation Office has rules about what can be sacrificed and how it affects fringe benefits tax.

The calculator on this site does not deduct salary sacrifice because it varies widely. If you use salary sacrifice, your take-home pay will be lower than the estimate, but you may save tax. For more details, see the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

The home page of this site is [the timesheet](/). You type your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and the number of hours per week (default 38). A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top. The calculator then shows your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual gross pay, plus an estimate of tax, Medicare, and super. It is a quick reference, not a binding determination.

For more detailed information, refer to the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for current rates, the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page for rules, and the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for industry averages from the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
